refractory_rationale: poor response after at least 3 days of macrolide therapy

recommendations.recommendation: Treat the case as suspected pediatric MPP and review pathogen results, imaging, and differential diagnoses together.
Recommend urgent clinician review for severe pneumonia features, oxygenation monitoring, complication assessment, and escalation planning.
Poor response or refractory-risk signals are present; review age-limited alternative antimicrobial options with a pediatric specialist. Do not auto-prescribe.
Follow up for persistent fever, worsening cough or dyspnea, falling oxygen saturation, poor oral intake, extrapulmonary symptoms, or delayed imaging recovery.

evidence_trace.statement: Pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia should be considered when a child has persistent fever and cough with compatible radiologic pneumonia, especially when pathogen testing such as PCR or serology supports Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection.
Follow-up should pay attention to persistent fever, worsening cough or dyspnea, decreasing oxygen saturation, poor oral intake, extrapulmonary symptoms, and delayed radiologic recovery.
Imaging findings such as lobar consolidation, multilobar involvement, atelectasis, pleural effusion, or necrotizing change provide important evidence for disease burden and complication assessment.

Persistent fever, poor clinical response after an adequate macrolide trial, elevated inflammatory markers, increased LDH, and significant radiologic involvement are commonly used warning signals for refractory or severe Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia.

Hypoxemia, respiratory distress, multilobar lung involvement, pleural effusion, atelectasis, rapid radiologic progression, or extrapulmonary complications suggest more severe disease and need closer monitoring.

Macrolides are commonly used first-line therapy for pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia. When resistance, intolerance, or poor response is suspected, alternative therapy should be reviewed by clinicians with attention to age limits, contraindications, local guidance, and antimicrobial stewardship.
